samples.question: A token starts on the cell with the thick black border. One step: the token leaves its cell in the direction that cell's arrow points at that moment, and that arrow then turns a quarter turn clockwise (up to right to down to left to up). The token carries on from the cell it entered under the same rule, and stops as soon as it steps off the grid. The drawn arrows are only the starting arrows, so any cell the token enters again has already turned. The four sides are labelled N, E, S and W. Which side does the token leave from? Answer with exactly one of: N, E, S, W.
